_comment: fcc Al from ABACUS's own H(R): ABACUS writes the sparse H(R) of its converged SCF (out_mat_hs2 1, abacus/al/INPUT), rsatb reads it as format 'abacus' and builds S from the same .orb file ABACUS used. ABACUS's H(R) is in Rydberg and in its own orbital order; both are converted on read. The atoms of conf.vasp must be listed in ABACUS's order. The primitive-cell file is folded onto a 3x3x3 tiling (27 atoms) at load and sampled on a 2x2x2 mesh -- a 6x6x6 sampling of the primitive zone -- one k-point per rank group (npar). Sized to run in minutes on 8 ranks: the 8 au Al orbitals give each atom ~200 neighbours and a 415 eV spectral span, so resolution and cell size are what cost.

tasks._comment: ONCV Al carries 11 valence electrons (2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1). The count is the trace of the occupation over the basis of the structure, with no spin factor: a spin-degenerate basis holds one spin, so 27 atoms x 11 / 2. Expect mu near 11.55 eV: exact diagonalization of this 6x6x6 sampling gives 11.547 eV, and the 16-sample stochastic trace lands within ~0.1 eV of it (11.635 eV in the run recorded in README.md). ABACUS's E_Fermi, 11.021 eV (data/al/abacus/E_Fermi_eV), is that of its 12x12x12 mesh (exact: 11.016 eV) -- a metal's Fermi level moves with the sampling, so mu has to come from the sampling it is used with.
Kubo-Greenwood conductivity at the Fermi level of this sampling (the fermi_level task above), both spins included.
